t: This is Flanders House, the surviving southern wing of Harcourt House, on the corner of Cavendish Square and Margaret Street. Thomas Archer, an English Baroque architect, designed the palatial house around 1722 for Simon Harcourt, a Tory politician who became Queen Anne's Lord High Chancellor. The main building was largely demolished in 1906, and this wing now stands as number 1A Cavendish Square. The eccentric fifth Duke of Portland, a recluse who had a maze of tunnels dug beneath Welbeck Abbey, died here in 1879.
